newsitem.title: CANADA: Oil interest in Saskatchewan outpaces last year.
newsitem.headline: Oil interest in Saskatchewan outpaces last year.

text.p: Energy industry excitement over light and heavy oil drilling prospects in Saskatchewan has driven revenues from land sales in the western Canadian province well beyond those reaped last year, the provincial Energy and Mines Department said on Thursday.
Saskatchewan said it has raised C$72.7 million selling petroleum and natural gas rights on government lands so far this year, a jump from C$44.5 million by the same period in 1996.

Saskatchewan, Canada's second-largest oil producing province behind Alberta, set a land-sale revenue record in 1994 when it took in about C$200 million. Revenues totalled C$140 million last year, its fourth-highest take.

"We're in a very good position, as far as we're concerned," Gordon Hutch, Saskatchewan's director of geology and petroleum lands, said in a telephone interview from Regina. "To be in amongst those numbers, it's very healthy."
A big factor behind the interest in Saskatchewan lands has been world oil prices, which were strong for most of the first half of this year, Hutch said.
The province said C$18.3 million flowed into its coffers at its June 10 land auction from the sale of 418 parcels of exploration acreage.
The Weyburn-Estevan region in the province's southeast -- site of active horizontal light oil drilling -- attracted the most interest, with successful bids of C$8.8 million.
The region has been the target of red-hot exploration interest after junior oil firm Berkley Petroleum Corp made a major discovery in the Red River Ordovician geological zone at Midale in late 1995.
However, acreage in the immediate Midale area, after attracting record bid prices until early this year, is now virtually gone, Hutch said.
At the most recent sale, the Kindersley-Kerrobert region in western Saskatchewan attracted the second-highest bid total at C$5.6 million.
The area is known mostly for heavy crude oil production, Canada fastest growing supply and the target of billions of dollors in project spending over the next decade in both Saskatchewan and Alberta.
Saskatchewan has also been an arena for corporate acquisitions over the past year as the race to produce more heavy oil has heated up.

Earlier this year, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd beat out Talisman Energy Inc in a battle to take over the large and former government-owned heavy oil producer Wascana Energy Inc. CanOxy paid about C$2 billion to acquire Wascana.

Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said last week it planned to offer about C$413 million to acquire CS Resources Ltd, which has a big enhanced heavy oil recovery operation in west central Saskatchewan. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
